title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) of the Brain with and without Contrast
description: Medicare coverage criteria for diagnostic brain MRI. Requires documented focal neurological deficit, new onset seizure, intractable cognitive decline with rapid progression, suspected demyelinating disease (MS), or persistent progressive headache accompanied by focal neurological signs.

criteria.name: Focal Neurological Deficit or New Onset Seizure
criteria.description: Clinical examination documenting objective focal neurological deficit (cranial neuropathy, hemiparesis, visual field loss, ataxia) or new-onset unprovoked seizure.
criteria.clinical_intent: Validate neurological indication for parenchymal evaluation
criteria.source_text_excerpt: In addition, neck MRI may be useful for the management of conditions involving the neck, including lesions involving the mouth, throat or neck; suspicious masses/tumors found on another imaging modality that needs additional clarification; neck masses or lymphadenopathy; infections of the face, neck or neck spaces involving any of the fascial planes; neurological conditions such as Bell’s palsy, hemifacial spasm or other neuropathies; and suspected thyroid or parathyroid neoplasms.

criteria.name: Progressive Headache with Red Flags or Abnormal Exam
criteria.description: Headache with progressive severity, nocturnal awakening, papilledema on fundoscopy, or worsening with Valsalva maneuver.
criteria.source_text_excerpt: Sinus MRI may be required to detect abnormalities and conditions such as rhinosinusitis with suspicion of fungal infections, clinical suspicion of orbital or intracranial complications, suspected mass based upon exam, nasal endoscopy or previous imaging and for conditions such as anosmia or osteomyelitis.

criteria.name: Typical Chronic Stable Headache Without Red Flags Exclusion
criteria.description: Brain MRI requested for long-standing typical tension headache or stable migraine without change in pattern or focal deficits.
criteria.clinical_intent: Exclude neuroimaging for typical stable non-red-flag headaches
criteria.source_text_excerpt: CT scanning remains the study of choice for the imaging evaluation of acute and chronic inflammatory diseases of the sinonasal cavities.
